reviewScope: All seven established coding exercises in chapter five, thirty-five independently authored language bodies, exact floating-point limits, signed/packed-byte bindings, independent oracles and mutation observations. The conceptual Debugger reference is classified separately; it is not an eighth executable problem.

questions.algorithm: Clear an inclusive interval with a width mask, then OR the fitting replacement shifted to low.
questions.review: Signed 32-bit words are treated as fixed patterns in every language. The fitting-insertion precondition is explicit. The full-width interval and bit 31 are valid and do not perform a 32-bit shift by 32. Every inclusive interval is exercised with zero, full and random fitting replacements. Negative insertion is permitted only for width 32.

questions.algorithm: Emit at most 31 digits by exact doubling and subtracting each units bit.
questions.review: The point counts toward the 32-character limit. Binary64 input rather than an exact decimal rational is explicit. Powers of two at 2^-31 and 2^-32 enforce the boundary, and 0.1 returns ERROR. C#/Java use builders, C++ appends chars, Python/JavaScript collect digits then join; O(b) construction matches every implementation.

questions.algorithm: Sliding bit window containing at most one zero.
questions.review: The right endpoint visits all 32 bits, and left advances until a second zero is excluded. Word boundaries, all-zero/all-one words, sign-bit-only words and separated/adjacent zeros are covered. The independent oracle tries each possible flip and counts textual runs.

questions.algorithm: Carry the lowest set-bit run upward, repack remaining ones low, and use 31-bit complementation to reverse the search for the predecessor.
questions.review: Zero is only an internal no-successor case, not an admitted positive input. Wider arithmetic prevents overflow before checking the 31-bit maximum. Output is [smaller,larger] with independent -1 sentinels. The oracle uses constrained digit search and is cross-checked against exhaustive integer enumeration on a bounded domain.

questions.algorithm: XOR the two 32-bit patterns, then clear the lowest set bit once per counted difference.
questions.review: Every actual implementation clears bits rather than scanning all positions, matching its O(k), k<=32 explanation. Negative values have exactly 32 bits. The independent reference compares individual positions, including the sign bit. Zero versus minus one yields 32.

questions.algorithm: Mask even and odd positions separately, move each group into its paired positions, and OR.
questions.review: All sixteen adjacent pairs are swapped simultaneously. Each one-bit input, sign-bit movement, alternating masks and random signed words are covered. The independent reference gathers each output bit from position i XOR 1. Involution and population-preservation properties are checked separately.

questions.algorithm: Intersect endpoint masks per affected byte and OR them into the original packed buffer.
questions.review: The same-byte case uses mask intersection; other pixels and rows retain their original bits. All languages receive native byte containers; Java observations normalize signed bytes to 0..255. C++ additionally checks original data pointer and length. Maximum screen dimensions, every endpoint pair in a two-byte row, nonzero initial data and repeated-drawing oracle properties are covered.

languageBindingReview.csharp: uint masks give logical shifts; explicit unchecked conversions preserve signed patterns. The insertion width-32 branch avoids C# shift-count wrapping. CountBitChanges subtracts only from a nonzero uint, so its decrement cannot underflow. BinaryFraction uses double and StringBuilder; neighbor arithmetic uses long; drawing receives byte[] and reports numeric bytes rather than JSON base64.
languageBindingReview.javascript: Bitwise operations operate on signed 32-bit values; >>> supplies logical shifts and unsigned normalization where needed. The insertion mask uses exact powers of two up to 2^32 before coercion, avoiding shift-count wrapping. Results are checked as signed 32-bit integers. BinaryFraction now collects digits in an array to justify linear output construction. Drawing uses Uint8Array; neighbor arithmetic stays exact below 2^32.
languageBindingReview.python: Inputs are masked to 32 bits before XOR counting and mask movement, and high-bit results are converted back by subtracting 2^32. Thus unbounded sign extension cannot create an infinite bit-clearing loop or an unsigned result alias. BinaryFraction accepts the actual float; the oracle uses as_integer_ratio. Drawing receives bytearray and checks the void result and original length.
languageBindingReview.cpp: Unsigned uint32_t patterns avoid signed-shift overflow. Insertion uses uint64_t so a shift by width 32 is defined. Conversion to a negative signed result first subtracts 2^32 in signed long long, then narrows only a value already in int range. This avoids relying on implementation-defined unsigned-to-signed narrowing. BinaryFraction uses double and string appends, neighbor intermediates use long long, and packed screen data uses vector<uint8_t>& with pointer preservation.
languageBindingReview.java: Insertion uses a 64-bit mask for width 32 and explicitly masks signed inputs into their 32-bit patterns. Pairwise swapping uses >>> rather than >>. Java's defined two's-complement int arithmetic makes lowest-bit clearing correct even when the sign bit is set. BinaryFraction uses double/StringBuilder; a LongUnaryOperator carries neighbor intermediates in long. Drawing masks/normalizes signed byte observations and returns void.
